# Frozen Story Following SQL fixture — 2026-10-02

The material-history reproduction reads the committed `story_following_v1.sql` bytes beside this document. It no longer needs a historical Git object, so a shallow CI checkout or source export can execute the same regression. There is no skip, fallback, dynamic fetch, or change to the reproduction's expectations.

The fixture was copied without edits from `supabase/source-proposals/story_following_v1.sql` at full source commit `670efb8ebd6b4d7fb09368d399fe5a2afbc03a77`. Its length is 39,594 bytes and its SHA-256 is `2d351c4d74e30462265bdd3855720d4b4e5531ef8b633b80a8b2e18d2f1cc90e`. The adjacent provenance manifest records the source commit, path and Git blob. Before executing the local SQL fixture, the test verifies the approved SHA-256, provenance, byte length and derived Git blob hash.

This is historical test input, not the current installation proposal or installation authority. Only test loading and fixture documentation changed; production SQL, News policy, gate expectations and workflows remain unchanged. Earlier qualification receipts remain intact.

The focused 23-test suite passes on Node 22 and Node 24. The frozen reproduction also passes on each runtime in a separate source export with no `.git` directory or historical objects and with parent-directory Git discovery blocked. It still witnesses full declared history producing Developing and a withdrawn first declaration incorrectly producing Breaking in the frozen SQL. The repaired-source regressions continue to refuse incomplete history.

Full suite:

```sh
node --test --test-concurrency=1 \
  tests/storyMaterialHistory.test.mjs tests/storyMaterialHistoryPackage.test.mjs \
  tests/storyFollowingCorrections.test.mjs tests/storyFollowingPackage.test.mjs
```

Export reproduction:

```sh
node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern='frozen670' \
  tests/storyMaterialHistory.test.mjs
```
